prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Redesign the photographed in-game Yorimichi skate pier into a flowing, beautiful coherent public skate space. Use the screenshots as BEFORE reference only. Create a skater-eye-height wide three-quarter architectural AFTER concept, painterly low-poly game graphics. Improve the disconnected boxed-off obstacles with wraparound smooth banks, quarter-to-bank hips and rolling terrain that naturally feed a seven-stair handrail/hubba line and a separate four-stair and manual-pad line, plenty of speed/run-in/run-out. Beyond, show the elevated bowl as sculpted rolling landform with skateable outer skirts instead of blank vertical walls, with warm tile coping and real deep curved inner walls. Central smooth low rollers connect lines. Art direction: warm ivory concrete, sage-grey transitions, terracotta flowing paving ribbons and stair cheeks, red metal rails, bronze fence, dark warm timber canopy, curved low concrete seats and clustered coastal grasses kept outside skating trajectories. Subtle clean slab joints and absolutely no huge patchy tan triangle artefacts. Flowing composition with clear spaces of rest and movement; new ramps must blend tangentially into ground. Keep blue sea and autumn Japanese coast. No UI, annotations, text, crowds or graffiti. Convincing buildable shapes, not impossible intersecting ramps.
